record.title: Garaschuk's conjecture on fractional triangle decompositions
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices and minimum degree at least $\frac{3}{4}n$. **Garaschuk's conjecture.** If $n$ is large enough, then $G$ is fractionally $K_3$-decomposable. Fractional triangle decomposability is a relaxation of an actual triangle decomposition, and this conjecture would provide the fractional decomposition threshold needed in approaches to Nash-Williams' conjecture. The source presents it as a conjecture and identifies Garaschuk's result as the best known result towards Nash-Williams' conjecture, so its resolution status should be checked against the cited work.
record.source_name: François Dross, “Fractional triangle decompositions in graphs with large minimum degree”, arXiv:1503.08191 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.08191

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2015). “The best known result towards proving Conjecture was established by Garaschuk .”

record.title: Nešetřil–Ossona de Mendez conjecture on bounded tree-depth components in 3-colorings of planar graphs
record.statement:
A **monochromatic component** is a connected component induced by vertices receiving the same color in a vertex coloring. The **tree-depth** of a graph is the minimum height of a rooted forest whose closure contains the graph.

**Nešetřil–Ossona de Mendez conjecture.** There exists a constant $t$ such that every planar graph has a vertex coloring with 3 colors in which every monochromatic component has tree-depth at most $t$.

The conjecture is refuted: the construction of $G_3$ in the paper gives planar graphs for which every 3-coloring has a monochromatic component containing a path of arbitrarily large length, and hence of arbitrarily large tree-depth.
record.source_name: Chun-Hung Liu and Sang-il Oum, “Partitioning H-minor free graphs into three subgraphs with no large components”, arXiv:1503.08371 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.08371

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2015); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Path-factor existence conjecture for graphs without small odd paths
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$, and let $G$ be a graph. For a graph $H$, let $\mathcal{C}(H)$ be the set of components of $H$; for $i\geq 1$, let $\mathcal{C}_i(H)=\{C\in\mathcal{C}(H)\mid |V(C)|=i\}$ and let $c_i(H)=|\mathcal{C}_i(H)|$. A **$\{P_2,P_{2k+1}\}$-factor** is a spanning subgraph whose components are copies of $P_2$ or $P_{2k+1}$. **Path-factor existence conjecture.** If

$$
\sum_{0\leq i\leq k-1}c_{2i+1}(G-X)\leq \frac{4k+6}{8k+3}|X|
$$

for all $X\subseteq V(G)$, then $G$ has a $\{P_2,P_{2k+1}\}$-factor. The conjecture extends the corresponding sufficient conditions known for $k=1$ and $k=2$. For $k\geq 3$ divisible by $3$, examples show that the analogous bound with an additional constant term cannot guarantee such a factor, while the conjecture proposes that removing this constant term suffices in every case.
record.source_name: Yoshimi Egawa and Michitaka Furuya, “The existence of a path-factor without small odd paths”, arXiv:1503.08556 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.08556

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2015).

record.title: Conjecture on conjugacy of cuspidal types
record.statement: Let $G$ be an isometry group over a non-archimedean field, and let cuspidal types be representations of compact open subgroups used to construct irreducible cuspidal representations by compact induction. **Cuspidal-type conjugacy conjecture.** Two cuspidal types are conjugate if and only if their compactly induced representations are isomorphic. This is the expected uniqueness statement for cuspidal types; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Daniel Skodlerack and Shaun Stevens, “Intertwining semisimple characters for p-adic classical groups”, arXiv:1503.08882 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.08882

record.title: The bounded-degree transversal conjecture for uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $k\ge 2$, and let $H$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges. Write $\tau(H)$ for its transversal number and $\Delta(H)$ for its maximum degree. **The bounded-degree transversal conjecture.** If $\Delta(H)\le 3$, then

$$
\tau(H)\le \frac{n}{k}+\frac{m}{6}.
$$

The conjecture extends the known cases for $k=2,3$ and addresses the remaining bounded-degree case; the paper notes that the corresponding inequality can fail when $k\ge 4$ and $\Delta(H)\ge 4$.
record.source_name: Michael A. Henning and Anders Yeo, “Transversals in 4-Uniform Hypergraphs”, arXiv:1504.02650 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.02650

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

record.title: The linear 4-uniform hypergraph transversal conjecture
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a $4$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges. Recall that $H$ is **linear** if every two edges intersect in at most one vertex, and let $\tau(H)$ denote its transversal number. **The linear transversal conjecture.** If $H$ is linear, then

$$
\tau(H)\le \frac{n}{4}+\frac{m}{6}.
$$

The paper presents this as a proposed extension of its bounded-degree result. It is motivated by the failure of the same bound for some hypergraphs of maximum degree at least $4$, while linearity rules out repeated intersections between pairs of edges.
record.source_name: Michael A. Henning and Anders Yeo, “Transversals in 4-Uniform Hypergraphs”, arXiv:1504.02650 (2015).
record.references:

record.title: The spectral characterization of geodesic growth for right-angled Coxeter groups on trees
record.statement: Let $T$ and $T'$ be trees. Assume that they are simultaneously co-spectral, their complements are co-spectral, and their line graphs are co-spectral. **Geodesic-growth conjecture.** Then $T$ and $T'$ have the same geodesic growth, meaning that the associated right-angled Coxeter groups $G(T)$ and $G(T')$ have the same geodesic growth series. The conjecture asks whether these three spectral data determine geodesic growth for right-angled Coxeter groups based on trees; the paper establishes examples supporting the question but does not resolve the general implication.
record.source_name: Laura Ciobanu and Alexander Kolpakov, “Geodesic growth of right-angled Coxeter groups based on trees”, arXiv:1504.02774 (2020).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.02774

record.title: Non-polynomial growth for k-dominating independent sets in incidence graphs of projective planes
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the family of incidence graphs of projective planes, and let $\text{mi}_k(n,\mathcal{F})$ denote the maximum number of $k$-dominating independent sets among $n$-vertex graphs in this family.

**Projective-plane incidence-graph conjecture.** The function $\text{mi}_k(n,\mathcal{F})$ is not bounded above by any polynomial in $n$.

This addresses the growth-rate alternatives posed for structured graph families and predicts superpolynomially many $k$-dominating independent sets in incidence graphs of projective planes. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Zoltán Lóránt Nagy, “On the number of k-dominating independent sets”, arXiv:1504.03224 (2015).

record.title: Classification conjecture for admissible anti-automorphisms of affine Hecke algebras
record.statement:
Let ${\mathcal H}$ be the affine Hecke algebra, with parameter ${\mathbf q}$, extended torus ${\mathcal T}$, and elements $\theta_x$ for $x\in X$. An automorphism $\kappa$ of ${\mathcal H}$ is **admissible** if it fixes ${\mathbf q}$ and each $T_w$, and satisfies $\kappa({\mathcal I}_a)\subseteq {\mathcal I}_{\hat\kappa(a)}$ for every $a\in{\mathcal T}$; here $\hat\kappa:{\mathcal T}\times{\mathbb C}^{\times}\to{\mathcal T}\times{\mathbb C}^{\times}$ is the induced map on the spectrum of the center. The operations $\bullet$ and $\star$ are admissible.

**Classification conjecture.** If $\kappa$ is an admissible involutive anti-automorphism, then:

1. If $\hat\kappa(a)=a$ for all $a\in{\mathcal T}$, then
 
$$
\kappa(\theta_x)=\theta_x^\bullet
$$

 for all $x\in X$.
2. If $\hat\kappa(a)=a^{-1}$ for all $a\in{\mathcal T}$, then
 
$$
\kappa(\theta_x)=\theta_x^\star
$$

 for all $x\in X$.

The conjecture proposes that the action of an admissible involutive anti-automorphism on the Bernstein elements $\theta_x$ is determined by its induced action on the torus: the identity action gives the $\bullet$ operation, while inversion gives the $\star$ operation. It is motivated by the corresponding classification for graded affine Hecke algebras and the relationship between affine and graded Hecke algebras.
record.source_name: Dan Barbasch and Dan Ciubotaru, “Star operations for affine Hecke algebras”, arXiv:1504.04361 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.04361

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

record.title: Field-extension conjecture for square roots of cyclotomic units
record.statement:
Let $czeta_k$ and $czeta_m$ be primitive roots of unity. **Field-extension conjecture.**

$$
\sqrt{1+4\zeta_k}\in\mathbb Q\left(\zeta_m\right)\Longleftrightarrow k=1\text{ and }5\mid m\text{ or }k=2\text{ and }3\mid m.
$$

Only the implication from left to right is open; the reverse implication is established in the paper. The conjecture characterizes when the relevant quadratic extension is already contained in a cyclotomic field and is used to determine convergence behavior of the generalized Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction at roots of unity.
record.source_name: Emil-Alexandru Ciolan and Robert Axel Neiss, “Convergence properties of the classical and generalized Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction”, arXiv:1504.06482 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.06482

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

record.title: Harutyunyan's acyclic-set conjecture for planar oriented graphs
record.statement: Let an **oriented graph** be a digraph without loops and multiple arcs, and let an **acyclic set** be a set of vertices inducing a subgraph with no directed cycles. **Harutyunyan's conjecture.** Every planar oriented graph of order $n$ has an acyclic set of size at least $\frac{3n}{5}$. The conjecture is refuted by the paper's construction of oriented planar graphs whose maximum acyclic set has size at most $\lceil \frac{n+1}{2} \rceil$.
record.source_name: Kolja Knauer, Petru Valicov and Paul S. Wenger, “Planar digraphs without large acyclic sets”, arXiv:1504.06726 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.06726

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2015). “However, the following remains open: [Albertson and Berman ] Every simple undirected planar graph of order $n$ has an induced forest of order at least $\frac{n}{2}$.”

record.title: The winding-number-zero extinction-time conjecture for curve diffusion flow
record.statement:
Let a curve diffusion flow start from a smooth immersed curve with winding number zero, and let its initial length be $L$. Let $T_{\mathrm{flow}}$ denote its maximal existence time, and let $T_{\mathrm{eight}}(L)$ denote the existence time of a self-similarly shrinking figure eight with initial length $L$. **Extinction-time conjecture.** The maximal existence time satisfies

$$
T_{\mathrm{flow}}\leq T_{\mathrm{eight}}(L).
$$

The conjecture proposes that the self-similar figure eight gives the largest possible existence time among flows starting from curves with winding number zero; the source presents this as a heuristic motivated by the generic development of curvature singularities, but gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Maureen Edwards, Alexander Gerhardt-Bourke, James McCoy, Glen Wheeler and Valentina-Mira Wheeler, “The shrinking figure eight and other solitons for the curve diffusion flow”, arXiv:1505.02978 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.02978

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

record.title: Dvořák's conjecture on coloring squares of girth-five planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph with girth $5$, let $\Delta$ denote its maximum degree, and let $M$ be a constant. The **Dvořák conjecture.** There exists some constant $M$ such that every planar graph $G$ with girth $5$ and maximum degree at least $M$ satisfies

$$
\Delta(G^2)\le\Delta+2.
$$

Here $G^2$ is the square of $G$ and $\Delta(G^2)$ denotes its maximum degree. This conjecture concerns the remaining high-degree, girth-five case after known results for larger girth; the supplied text gives no resolution, so it is open.
record.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston and Bobby Jaeger, “List-coloring the Squares of Planar Graphs without 4-Cycles and 5-Cycles”, arXiv:1505.03197 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.03197

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2015). “Although the conjecture remains open in general, Havet et al.\ showed that the conjectured upper bound holds asymptotically, i.e., $\chi(G^2) \le \frac{3}{2}\Delta + o(\Delta)$.”

record.title: The age conjecture for counting G-fields
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field, let $G$ be a finite group, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional faithful representation of $G$ over $K$. Let $N_{G,V,K}(B)$ count isomorphism classes of $G$-fields $L/K$ with $V$-discriminant $D_L^V\le B$. Let $\operatorname{age}(G)$ be the minimum of the age function on $G\setminus\{1\}$, and let $\upsilon(G)$ be the number of nontrivial $K$-conjugacy classes with minimum age. **The age conjecture.** If $K$ is sufficiently large, then 
$$
N_{G,V,K}(B)\sim CB^{1/\operatorname{age}(G)}(\log B)^{\upsilon(G)}.
$$
 This is proposed as a representation-theoretic analogue of Malle's conjecture, with age replacing index; the source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Takehiko Yasuda, “Manin's conjecture vs. Malle's conjecture”, arXiv:1505.04555 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04555

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

record.title: The generalized Malle conjecture for linear group actions
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and let $G$ act faithfully and linearly on $V=\mathbb{A}_K^d$, with the associated map $\overline{V}\to\overline{X}=\overline{V}/G$ étale in codimension one. Let $N(G,V,B)$ count $G$-fields with extended $V$-discriminant at most $B$, and let $\operatorname{age}(G)$ be the minimum age of a nontrivial element of $G$. Let $\upsilon(G)$ be the number of youngest $K$-conjugacy classes. **The generalized Malle conjecture.** If $K$ is sufficiently large, then 
$$
N(G,V,B)\sim CB^{1/\operatorname{age}(G)}(\log B)^{\upsilon(G)-1}.
$$
 This extends Malle's predicted exponent from permutation representations to general faithful linear actions; the source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Takehiko Yasuda, “Manin's conjecture vs. Malle's conjecture”, arXiv:1505.04555 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04555

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

record.title: Chen–Dehmer–Shi's extremal entropy conjecture for trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with $n$ vertices. Let $S_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\lceil n/2\rceil}$ be the balanced double star, and let $CS(n,t)$ denote a comet; write $t_0$ for the parameter specified by the conjecture. The entropy under consideration is $I_{f^n_2}$.

**Chen–Dehmer–Shi's conjecture.** The balanced double star and the comet $CS(n,t_0)$ attain the maximum and minimum values of $I_{f^n_2}(T)$, respectively.

The conjecture is motivated by the preceding comparison between the star, path and balanced double star and by the proposed extremal role of the comet. The source does not provide a proof or a resolution.
record.source_name: Xueliang Li and Meiqin Wei, “A survey of recent results in (generalized) graph entropies”, arXiv:1505.04658 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04658

record.title: The Dedekind-domain containment conjecture for idempotent plethories
record.statement: Let $D$ be a Dedekind domain of characteristic zero with quotient field $K$. **The Dedekind-domain containment conjecture.** Every idempotent $D$-plethory is contained in $K[e]$, or, equivalently, ${\operatorname{Int}}(D)$ is the largest idempotent $D$-plethory and is therefore the epimorphic hull of the trivial $D$-plethory. This conjecture addresses the classification of idempotent plethories and the existence of an epimorphic hull of the trivial plethory for Dedekind domains.
record.source_name: Jesse Elliott, “Idempotent plethories”, arXiv:1505.06493 (2025).

record.title: Exact-value conjecture for the multi-nut caching game
record.statement:
Consider the caching game with $k=j\ge2$, where the hider caches $k$ nuts, the searcher aims to find all $k$, and the parameters include $n$ holes and search depth $h$. The source proves the upper bound

$$
\text{value}\le\frac{h^k}{{n+k-1\choose k}}.
$$

**Multi-nut exact-value conjecture.** If

$$
k=j\ge2,\qquad\frac{k+1}{k-1}\le h\le\frac nk,
$$

then the value of the game is

$$
\frac{h^k}{{n+k-1\choose k}}.
$$

The conjecture extends the two-nut analysis; the source suggests that the integral-depth case may be easier but does not prove the full statement.
record.source_name: Endre Csóka, “Limit theory of discrete mathematics problems”, arXiv:1505.06984 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.06984

record.title: Diadem–nucleus characterization of König–Egerváry graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $
u(G)$ denote its maximum matching size, and let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number. Write $\mathrm{diadem}(G)$ for the union of all critical independent sets of $G$, and $\mathrm{nucleus}(G)$ for their intersection.

**Diadem–nucleus conjecture.** If

$$
\left\vert \mathrm{diadem}(G)\right\vert +\left\vert \mathrm{nucleus}(G)\right\vert =2\alpha(G),
$$

then $G$ is a König–Egerváry graph, that is, $\left\vert V(G)\right\vert=\alpha(G)+\nu(G)$.

This proposes a sufficient condition for a graph to be König–Egerváry, linking the union and intersection of its critical independent sets to its independence number. The supplied text does not indicate whether the problem has been resolved.
record.source_name: Adi Jarden, Vadim E. Levit and Eugen Mandrescu, “Monotonic Properties of Collections of Maximum Independent Sets of a Graph”, arXiv:1506.00249 (2015).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.00249

record.title: Bidirectional tunnel classification for the simplest bomb shape
record.statement:
A **bidirectional tunnel** is a tunnel whose motion occurs in two directly opposite directions. For the simplest bomb shape, only the wall hit by the particle is erased, and the particle starts with an initial angle of movement. **Bidirectional tunnel conjecture.** The only bidirectional tunnels are those corresponding to an initial angle of movement which is an integer multiple of 
$$
\frac{\pi}{4}.
$$
 The paper reports that no other examples were found in simulation, while related variants exhibit additional bidirectional tunnels.
record.source_name: Edward Newkirk, “Billiards with Bombs”, arXiv:1506.00683 (2015).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.00683

record.title: Strong diameter conjecture for direct powers of finite groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $G^n$ denote its $n$-th direct power, and let $D(G^n)$ denote the diameter with respect to a generating set, using words in that set. Write ${\mathrm{rank}}(G)$ for the minimum size of a generating set of $G$. **Strong diameter conjecture.** The diameter $D(G^n)$ is at most

$$
n\bigl(|G|-{\mathrm{rank}}(G)\bigr).
$$

The bound would give a linear, rather than exponential, estimate in $n$ for direct powers; it is proposed as a stronger form of the accompanying assertion concerning a suitable minimum generating set.
record.source_name: Nasim Karimi, “Diameter of a direct power of a finite group”, arXiv:1506.02695 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02695

record.title: Weak diameter conjecture for direct powers of finite groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $G^n$ denote its $n$-th direct power, and let $A$ be a generating set of minimum size for $G^n$. Write ${\mathrm{rank}}(G)$ for the minimum size of a generating set of $G$, and let ${\mathrm{diam}}(G^n,A)$ be the diameter with respect to $A$. **Weak diameter conjecture.** There exists a generating set $A$ for $G^n$ of minimum size such that

$$
{\mathrm{diam}}(G^n,A)\leq n\bigl(|G|-{\mathrm{rank}}(G)\bigr).
$$

This is the weaker companion to the assertion for the diameter with respect to any generating set, and is intended to provide a polynomial bound for the diameter of direct powers.
record.source_name: Nasim Karimi, “Diameter of a direct power of a finite group”, arXiv:1506.02695 (2015).

record.title: Lawson–Simons conjecture for submanifolds in spheres
record.statement:
Let $F_{0}:M^{n}\to\mathbb{S}^{n+q}$ be an $n$-dimensional closed submanifold satisfying

$$
|h|^{2}<2\sqrt{n-1},
$$

where $h$ is the second fundamental form. **Lawson–Simons conjecture.** The mean curvature flow with initial value $F_{0}$ converges to a round point or a totally geodesic sphere. In particular, $M_{0}$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{S}^{n}$. The source presents this as a special case motivated by the minimum of the pinching function and explicitly states that the Lawson–Simons conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Li Lei and Hongwei Xu, “Mean curvature flow of arbitrary codimension in spheres and sharp differentiable sphere theorem”, arXiv:1506.06371 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.06371

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2015). “Up to now, the Lawson-Simons conjecture is still open.”

record.title: The extremal number conjecture for powers of balanced rooted trees
record.statement:
Let $(T,R)$ be a balanced rooted tree, let $T^p$ be the graph formed from the union of $p$ distinct labelled copies of $T$ that agree on the roots $R$ and are otherwise disjoint, and let $\rho_T$ denote the rooted density of $T$. **Extremal number conjecture.** For any balanced rooted tree $(T,R)$,

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,T^p)=O_p\left(n^{2-1/\rho_T}\right).
$$

The preceding lower-bound result gives $\operatorname{ex}(n,T^p)=\Omega(n^{2-1/\rho_T})$ for balanced rooted trees, so this conjecture would determine the order of magnitude of the extremal number. It is posed as the corresponding upper bound and remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Boris Bukh and David Conlon, “Rational exponents in extremal graph theory”, arXiv:1506.06406 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.06406

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2015).

record.title: EKR conjecture for depth-two claws
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a depth-two claw with $n$ leaves. For a positive integer $r$, let $G$ be $r$-EKR when no pairwise intersecting family of independent sets of size $r$ in $G$ is larger than the largest $r$-star, where an $r$-star is the family of such sets containing a fixed vertex.

**Depth-two-claw EKR conjecture.** Let $n$ and $r$ be positive integers, with $n > r$, and let $G$ be a depth-two claw with $n$ leaves. Then $G$ is $r$-EKR.

The conjecture is motivated by the construction of a non-star intersecting family showing that the boundary case $r=n$ fails, together with the paper's theorem for related depth-two claw cases. Its general status is left open in the source.
record.source_name: Carl Feghali, Matthew Johnson and Daniel Thomas, “Erdős-Ko-Rado Theorems for a Family of Trees”, arXiv:1506.07741 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.07741

record.title: Odlyzko–Stanley conjecture on the growth of $p$-Stanley sequences
record.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime. A **$p$-Stanley sequence** $S_p(A)=a_1,a_2,\ldots$ is generated greedily from a $p$-free set $A$ of nonnegative integers, by adjoining at each step the smallest larger integer that preserves $p$-freeness. **Odlyzko–Stanley conjecture.** Every $p$-Stanley sequence satisfies one of the following two growth laws:

$$
a_n=\Theta\left(n^{\log_{p-1}p}\right)
$$

or

$$
a_n=\Theta\left(\frac{n^{(p-1)/(p-2)}}{(\log n)^{1/(p-2)}}\right).
$$

The first law is the modular, digit-structured behavior, while the second is the conjectured chaotic behavior motivated by the authors' heuristic. The source gives no resolution of this conjecture.
record.source_name: Mehtaab Sawhney and Jonathan Tidor, “Two classes of modular p-Stanley sequences”, arXiv:1506.07941 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.07941

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2015). “This conjecture has since been disproved.”

record.title: The digital capacity conjecture for the analogue communication network
record.statement: Let the communication network be the one depicted in figure labelled `analogue`, and let its digital capacity denote the largest rate achievable using digital communication. **Digital capacity conjecture.** The digital capacity of this network is strictly less than $1$. The paper presents this as an open conjecture motivated by the gap between the known lower and upper bounds for the two communication models.

record.title: Goubko's BFS-tree conjecture for distance spectral radius
record.statement: Let a tree degree sequence be fixed, and let $BFS(\mathbf{d})$ denote the breadth-first-search (greedy) tree generated by it. The **BFS-tree conjecture for distance spectral radius.** The tree $BFS(\mathbf{d})$ has the minimum distance spectral radius among all trees with degree sequence $\mathbf{d}$. This generalizes the conjecture of Stevanovic and Ilic for Volkmann trees; its status is not resolved in the source.

record.title: Goubko's BFS-tree conjecture for terminal distance spectral radius
record.statement: Let $\mathbf{d}$ be a tree degree sequence, and let $BFS(\mathbf{d})$ denote its breadth-first-search (greedy) tree. For a graph $G$, let $RD(G)$ be its terminal distance matrix, and let the **terminal distance spectral radius** be the spectral radius of $RD(G)$. The **BFS-tree conjecture for terminal distance spectral radius.** The tree $BFS(\mathbf{d})$ has the minimum terminal distance spectral radius among all trees with degree sequence $\mathbf{d}$. The paper establishes lower and upper bounds whose relative gap is numerically at most $3\%$, but the exact minimum statement remains open.

record.title: Minimal-denominator conjecture for relative extremal projectors
record.statement:
Let ${\mathfrak g}$ be a reductive Lie algebra, ${\mathfrak l}$ a Levi subalgebra, and $P({\mathfrak g},{\mathfrak l})$ the relative extremal projector. Let

$$
D({\mathfrak g},{\mathfrak l}):= \prod_{i=1}^\infty \mathop{\rm HC}\nolimits_{\mathfrak l}^{-1}\biggl(\prod_{\alpha\in\Delta({\mathfrak u}^+)}(H_\alpha+i)^{\rho_{\mathfrak g}}\biggr)
$$

be the lower-bound denominator from the preceding proposition. **Minimal-denominator conjecture.** There is a formula for $P({\mathfrak g},{\mathfrak l})$ with total denominator $D({\mathfrak g},{\mathfrak l})$. The conjecture asserts that the lower bound for the total denominator is achievable, giving a formula with the smallest denominator predicted by the proposition.
record.source_name: Charles H. Conley and Mark R. Sepanski, “Factorizations of relative extremal projectors”, arXiv:1507.02587 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.02587

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

record.title: The minimum-degree conjecture for distance-preserving graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree. A graph is **distance preserving** if it has an isometric subgraph of every order from $1$ to $n$.

**Minimum-degree conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(G)>n/2,
$$

then $G$ is distance preserving.

Nussbaum and Esfahanian proved the stronger minimum-degree condition $\delta(G)\geq 2n/3-1$, so the conjecture remains open in the stated range.
record.source_name: Emad Zahedi, “Distance Preserving Graphs”, arXiv:1507.03615 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.03615

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

record.title: Uniqueness conjecture for the minimising matrix of $c_n$
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the set of all $n\times n$ lower triangular $(0,1)$-matrices with every diagonal entry equal to $1$, and let $c_n$ be the minimum of the smallest eigenvalues of $YY^T$ over $Y\in K_n$. For each $n\geq2$, let $Y_0\in K_n$ be the matrix with entries

$$
(Y_0)_{ij}=\begin{cases}0&\text{if }i<j,\\1&\text{if }i=j,\\frac{1-(-1)^{i+j}}{2}&\text{if }i>j.\end{cases}
$$

**Uniqueness conjecture.** There is a unique matrix $Y\in K_n$ such that the smallest eigenvalue of $YY^T$ is $c_n$. Equivalently, if the smallest eigenvalue of $YY^T$ equals $c_n$, then $Y=Y_0$.

The authors report finding no matrix other than $Y_0$ with this property for $n=2,3,\ldots,9$. The conjecture strengthens the preceding minimisation claim by asserting uniqueness, but the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Ercan Altınışık, Ali Keskin, Mehmet Yıldız and Murat Demirbüken, “On the Ilmonen-Haukkanen-Merikoski Conjecture”, arXiv:1507.05112 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.05112

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

record.title: Distance-regular graph extendability conjecture for diameter at least three
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a distance-regular graph of valency $k$, even order $v$, and diameter $D\geq 3$. Its **extendability** is the largest integer $t$ such that every matching of $t$ edges is contained in a perfect matching.

**Distance-regular graph extendability conjecture.** The extendability of $G$ is at least

$$
\left\lceil \frac{k}{2}\right\rceil-1.
$$

The paper identifies this as still open for strongly regular graphs, which are distance-regular graphs of diameter two; the conjecture concerns the stated diameter-at-least-three case and is presented as an open problem in the final remarks.
record.source_name: Sebastian M. Cioabă, Jack H. Koolen and Weiqiang Li, “Max-cut and extendability of matchings in distance-regular graphs”, arXiv:1507.06254 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.06254

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2015). “We make the following conjecture which is still open for strongly regular graphs .”

record.title: Tarjan's deque conjecture for online binary search trees
record.statement: Let ${\mathcal{A}}$ be an online binary search tree algorithm. Starting with any initial tree $T$ with $n$ elements, consider inserting or deleting the current minimum or maximum elements $m$ times. **Deque conjecture.** The cost of these operations is $O(m+n)$. This is one of the classical conjectures about the efficiency of splay trees and online binary search trees; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Parinya Chalermsook, Mayank Goswami, Laszlo Kozma, Kurt Mehlhorn and Thatchaphol Saranurak, “Pattern-avoiding access in binary search trees”, arXiv:1507.06953 (2015).

record.title: Minimum-degree refinement of the Barát–Thomassen conjecture
record.statement: Let $T$ be a fixed tree with maximum degree $\Delta_T$, and let $|E(T)|$ denote its number of edges. A graph is **$T$-decomposable** if its edges can be partitioned into sets each inducing a copy of $T$. **Minimum-degree refinement of the Barát–Thomassen conjecture.** There is a function $f$ such that every graph that is $f(\Delta_T)$-edge-connected, whose number of edges is divisible by $|E(T)|$, and whose minimum degree is at least $f(|E(T)|)$, is $T$-decomposable. This refinement seeks to replace the dependence on a large edge-connectivity bound by separate bounds involving the tree's maximum degree and size. The source presents it as a proposed refinement; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Julien Bensmail, Ararat Harutyunyan, Tien-Nam Le and Stéphan Thomassé, “Edge-partitioning a graph into paths: beyond the Barát-Thomassen conjecture”, arXiv:1507.08208 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.08208

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2015). “This conjecture was recently verified by the current authors and Merker .”

record.title: Polynomial bound for spherical codes with a negative interval and k positive inner products
record.statement:
Let $N_L(d)$ denote the maximum size of a spherical code in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose pairwise inner products belong to $L$. For $\beta$ and $k$ as in the conjecture, and for any real numbers $\alpha_1,\dotsc,\alpha_k$, set

$$
L=[-1,-\beta]\cup\{\alpha_1,\dotsc,\alpha_k\}.
$$

**Polynomial spherical-code conjecture.** Suppose $\alpha_1,\dotsc,\alpha_k$ are any $k$ real numbers. Then

$$
N_L(d)\leq c_{\beta,k}d^k.
$$

This extends the linear bound for a single allowed inner product and the constant bound for inner products in $[-1,-\beta]$. The conjectured degree-$k$ estimate is left open in the source.
record.source_name: Boris Bukh, “Bounds on equiangular lines and on related spherical codes”, arXiv:1508.00136 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.00136

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).

record.title: Cooper–Embree–Ha–Ha–Hoefel lower-bound conjecture for monomial ideals
record.statement:
Let $I$ be a monomial ideal, and let $\operatorname{big-height}(I)$ denote the maximum of the heights of the associated primes $P\in\operatorname{Ass}(I)$. Write $e=\operatorname{big-height}(I)$, and let $\alpha(I)$ and $\widehat\alpha(I)$ denote the initial degree and Waldschmidt constant of $I$, respectively. **Cooper–Embree–Ha–Ha–Hoefel's conjecture.**

$$
\widehat\alpha(I)\geq\frac{\alpha(I)+e-1}{e}.
$$
 This is a Chudnovsky-like lower bound for the Waldschmidt constant of a monomial ideal, extending the analogous proposed bound for ideals of points in projective space. The supplied text does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.

record.title: Zauner–Appleby conjecture on Weyl–Heisenberg SIC fiducials
record.statement:
Let $U_{\mathcal{Z}}$ be the Zauner unitary associated with the Zauner symplectic matrix

$$
\mathcal{Z}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

A **Weyl–Heisenberg SIC fiducial** is a fiducial vector generating a symmetric informationally complete measurement under Weyl–Heisenberg translations. **Zauner–Appleby conjecture.** In every $d$-dimensional Hilbert space, there exists a Weyl–Heisenberg SIC fiducial that is an eigenvector in the largest eigenspace of $U_{\mathcal{Z}}$. This symmetry prediction is supported by all dimensions in which exhaustive searches have been performed, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Hoan Bui Dang, “Studies of symmetries that give special quantum states the "right to exist"”, arXiv:1508.02703 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.02703

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).

record.title: Existence of non-$(0,d-1)$-scribable polytopes
record.statement: A $d$-polytope is a polytope of dimension $d$, and a polytope is **$(0,d-1)$-scribable** if it has a realization whose vertices lie on a sphere and whose facets are tangent to a concentric sphere. **The non-$(0,d-1)$-scribability conjecture.** For $d>3$, there are $d$-polytopes that are not $(0,d-1)$-scribable. The authors believe this is true but do not construct examples; projectively unique polytopes or polytopes with constrained realization spaces may provide a strategy, though the known families are essentially inscribable.
record.source_name: Hao Chen and Arnau Padrol, “Scribability problems for polytopes”, arXiv:1508.03537 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.03537

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).

record.title: Prime Coxeter number conjecture for dominant numbers of dual fundamental series
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be the simple Lie algebra considered in the topological ODE construction, with Coxeter number $h$, rank $n$, and dual fundamental series $\phi_{a;a}$ for $a\in\{1,\dots,n\}$. For each $a$, let $r_a$ be the smallest order of a scalar linear ODE with polynomial coefficients in $x$ satisfied by $\phi_{a;a}$; this ODE is called its dominant equation, and $r_a$ its dominant number. The point $x=0$ is a regular singularity of the dominant equation. **Prime Coxeter number conjecture.** If $h$ is prime, then

$$
r_1=\dots=r_n=h-1.
$$

The assertion predicts a uniform maximal value for the dominant numbers when the Coxeter number is prime. The supplied text does not indicate whether this claim has been proved or remains open.
record.source_name: Marco Bertola, Boris Dubrovin and Di Yang, “Simple Lie algebras and topological ODEs”, arXiv:1508.03750 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.03750

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).
